home.heroTitle: Innovation in pig traceability and identification
home.heroSubtitle: PIGTATTOO develops tattoo-based identification technologies to improve traceability, animal welfare and sustainability in the pig sector.
home.whatBody: PIGTATTOO is a Supra-regional Operational Group within the European Innovation Partnership (EIP-AGRI) that brings together producers, industry, technology centres and universities to develop and validate an innovative tattoo-based pig identification system. The goal is to improve traceability along the whole chain, reduce animal stress and provide reliable data to producers, slaughterhouses and consumers.
home.pillar1Body: Reliable, verifiable identification systems at every link of the pig value chain.
home.pillar2Body: Methods fully respectful of animal health and welfare
home.pillar3Body: A new paradigm with less material use and improved production efficiency
home.contactCtaBody: Get in touch with the PIGTATTOO team for more information.

project.title: The project
project.intro: PIGTATTOO represents a new paradigm in animal identification, covering the animal's entire life and enabling greater traceability, genetic improvement and production efficiency.
project.objectivesBody: The main objective of the Project is to introduce a new tattoo-based identification method for pigs that replaces current systems in a more affordable and efficient way, with digitalisation capabilities for management and traceability
project.methodologyBody: The Project methodology moves through successive testing phases as the innovative systems are developed and combined into the final animal identification solution.
project.timelineBody: The project runs from 2025 to 2029, from the call for proposals to final closure, covering technical development, field validation and final testing.

images.methodologyIntro: The diagram shows two development periods and a final testing and analysis phase.
methodologyItems: Period 1 (starting February 2026): initial knowledge-acquisition work — A1 Initial tests (mesh test) and A2 System, animal welfare and other requirements — plus Period 1 developments: A4 PIGTATTOO ink, A3 Image capture hardware and A3 Intermediate tests.
Period 2: developments — A5 Information coding system, A6 Tattoo application system and A7 Computer vision AI system. End of developments: September 2028.
Final phase: A8 Economic impact and replicability, A8 Testing and results phase, and A8 Animal welfare verification.

Dissemination milestones: initial dissemination of the Project launch; dissemination of results (tests and requirements); dissemination of results (end of Period 1, April 2027); dissemination of results (completed developments); dissemination of results (end of Project, April 2029).
Key dates: start February 2026; end of Period 1 April 2027; end of developments September 2028; end of Project April 2029.

a1.title: Initial component testing
a1.body: Preliminary validation of the technological components that make up the tattoo-based identification system.

a2.title: Definition of requirements, control and verification of the systems
a2.body: Definition of criteria and protocols to guarantee technical feasibility, animal welfare and food safety in the Project.

a3.title: Intermediate component testing and hardware development
a3.body: Development and intermediate testing of the hardware needed to apply and read the pig tattoo.

a4.title: Development of the Project tattoo ink
a4.body: Research and formulation of the specific ink for identifying tattoos in pigs.

a5.title: Information coding system
a5.body: Design of the coding system that will allow each animal's identity to be assigned and interpreted.

a6.title: Physical application system
a6.body: Development of the physical device responsible for applying the tattoo accurately and safely.

a7.title: Computer vision system for animal identification
a7.body: Creation of a computer vision based system for automatic tattoo reading.

a8.title: Piloting and final Project testing
a8.body: Real-environment validation of the full set of systems, final improvements and animal welfare assessment.
